image: A hypothetical demand and supply diagram for the market for tyres. The horizontal axis represents the quantity of tyres, and the vertical axis represents the price of tyres. An initial downward-sloping demand curve (D1) and an upward-sloping supply curve (S1) intersect at an initial equilibrium point, determining an initial equilibrium price (P1) and quantity (Q1). An increase in demand for cars, being a complementary good to tyres, would cause the demand curve for tyres to shift to the right, from D1 to D2. This shift would result in a new equilibrium point, with a higher equilibrium price (P2) and a higher equilibrium quantity (Q2) of tyres.

image: A hypothetical Production Possibility Curve (PPC) diagram. The horizontal axis represents the quantity of one type of good (e.g., consumer goods), and the vertical axis represents the quantity of another type of good (e.g., capital goods). An initial outward-bowed PPC (PPC1) shows the maximum combinations of these two goods an economy can produce with its given resources and technology. The destruction of roads, bridges, houses, and capital goods due to damaging weather represents a reduction in the economy's productive capacity and available resources. This would be depicted by an inward shift of the PPC, from PPC1 to PPC2, indicating that the economy can now produce fewer combinations of goods and services.
